rows.question: Why are vitamin D levels lower in obese individuals?
rows.answer: There is no consensus on the exact reasons why vitamin D levels are lower in obese individuals. The main hypothesis is that vitamin D, being fat-soluble, is absorbed by adipose tissue, which may lead to lower bioavailability of the vitamin in the bloodstream. Additionally, factors such as decreased exposure to sunlight due to lifestyle choices, including excessive screen time, may also contribute to lower vitamin D levels in this population. The relationship appears to be multifactorial, influenced by both metabolic processes and lifestyle factors.
